reason: Hypothesis A is more specific and testable: it defines a clear intervention (stepwise cooling profile to control precipitate size ~5–20 nm), a precise temperature range (600–800 °C), a measurable predicted outcome (20–30% higher plastic strain), and a decisive falsification rule. Hypothesis B is vaguer (e.g., 'potentially doubling' strain, broader 800–1500 °C range) and cites evidence (E2) that describes incoherent TiC dispersoids, not coherent nanoprecipitates, weakening its mechanistic grounding.
